title: Best Average Over k in a Row
statement:
You get an array nums of integers and a window length k. Look at every run of exactly k consecutive elements and return the highest average among them.

The answer is a floating-point number; any answer within 10⁻⁵ of the true value is accepted.

examples.why: The windows sum to 9, 7, 15, 3. The best is [8, 1, 6] with sum 15, so 15 / 3 = 5.
The single largest value is 10, but the window [10, -50] is terrible. [9, 9] wins.
All numbers are negative, so the best average is still negative. Starting the maximum at 0 would be wrong.

hints: All windows have the same length k, so the best average belongs to the window with the best sum.
Neighbouring windows share k − 1 elements. How does the sum change when the window slides one step?
Add the element that enters and subtract the one that leaves. Track the best sum, divide by k once at the end.

explain.intuition:
Dividing by the same k never changes which window is best, so this is really "find the largest sum of k consecutive elements". Summing every window from scratch costs O(k) each time.

When the window slides right by one, exactly one element enters and one leaves. So the new sum is the old sum plus the newcomer minus the one that dropped off: O(1) per step. It is the same trick as a rolling metric in a dashboard, like "requests in the last 60 seconds", that you update instead of recount.
steps: Sum the first k elements; call it sum and set best = sum.
For i from k to n − 1: sum += nums[i] − nums[i − k].
pitfalls: Starting best at 0. With all-negative input every window is below 0, so the answer would be wrong.
Subtracting nums[i − k + 1] instead of nums[i − k]. That is an off-by-one that silently gives windows of length k − 1.
Dividing inside the loop and comparing floats. It works, but dividing once at the end is simpler and exact until the last step.

solutions.title: Sum every window
solutions.idea: For each start, add up the k elements from there.

solutions.title: Sliding sum
solutions.idea: Keep the sum of the current window and update it in O(1) as it slides.

followups: The window may be any length of at least k. How would you find the best average then? (Hint: binary search on the answer.)
The numbers arrive as a stream. What do you need to keep in memory?
